Definition: from G303 and G3525; to become sober again, i.e. (figuratively) regain (one's) senses:--recover self.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: Paul prays that those who oppose themselves may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will. It is waking up sober — coming back to your senses after being caught in a trap you did not see, and finding the way out.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for coming back to your senses carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the escape — the snare of the devil, and the recovery God gives.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
